summary: Audit the existing player-stats engine, benchmark GameChanger/MaxPreps, and design season accumulation + player/parent access

understand.models: packages/database/prisma/schema.prisma lines 2159-2498: RosterPlayer (per-game appearance, nullable personId/teamId), SportsPerson (persistent athlete), Team (program), PlayerSeasonStat (season aggregate), PlayerCareerStat (career)
understand.finalizeWired: YES - apps/api/src/sports/sports.service.ts:3344. Called POST-COMMIT in setStatus() when status=FINAL. Wrapped try/catch (fail-open). Gated SPORTS_PLAYER_STATS flag. Idempotent via game.stats.statsFinalizedAt marker inside transaction.
understand.linkingUX: MANUAL ONE-TAP. apps/web RosterPanel.tsx:318-370 shows LinkAthleteButton on every roster row. One-tap sends name to POST /sports/games/:id/roster/:rosterPlayerId/link. Server find-or-create SportsPerson. NO auto-match by number. Operator must link every row per game.
understand.accessSurface: NOT SURFACED. getAthleteCareer (sports-stats.service.ts:840) exists, wired via SportsService (line 3383), exposed GET /sports/athletes/:id/career (sports.controller.ts:1063-1080). NO web page. No public link. Admin-only (SPORTS_PLAYER_STATS gated). Player/parent cannot reach it - needs endpoint URL and personId never provided.
understand.seasonDefinition: deriveSeason() (sports-stats.service.ts:414-424): game.startedAt YEAR or game.createdAt YEAR or NOW YEAR. Yields string like 2026. NO Season model. NO academic-calendar (2025-26). Single calendar year. Winter sports straddle New Year, split into two season rows.
understand.gameLog: PER-GAME LINES PRESERVED. RosterPlayer rows persist per game (schema 2159-2190). Each: game_id + person_id + team_id + stats (JSON). Historical log reconstructable by querying RosterPlayer WHERE person_id ORDER BY game.createdAt. No dedicated box-score table; stats are flexible JSON per row.
gaps: ZERO PUBLIC SURFACE: getAthleteCareer built but not exposed anywhere players/parents reach it. No athlete profile page, no public link, no share-to-parent.
NO GAME-LOG VIEW: Even if accessible, no per-game stat lines chronologically shown.
MANUAL LINKING PER GAME: Operator must LinkAthleteButton every roster row every game. No bulk-link-by-name, no CSV auto-match, no retroactive link.
SEASON NOT SPORTS-AWARE: Calendar year only, not academic season (2025-26). Winter sports straddle New Year, split aggregates.
NO MILESTONE/RECORD WIRING: StatRecord/StatMilestoneDef/PlayerMilestone tables exist but not wired to finalizeGameStats. No record celebrations.
EXPORT/SHARE NOT WIRED: No CSV download, no printable summary, no email-to-parent.
MULTI-TENANT TEAM IDENTITY: RosterPlayer.teamId is nullable. Game.homeTeam/awayTeam are plain strings (not Team FK). Cannot auto-match across games by team+number.

products.name: GameChanger (Dick's Sporting Goods)
products.howStatsWork: The category leader for youth baseball/softball + 11 other sports. A volunteer scorekeeper (parent/coach) records play-by-play in the app during the game; 150+ stats + spray charts are auto-derived from the plays, and if the game is also live-streamed, highlight clips are auto-cut per play. Persistent ATHLETE IDENTITY: each kid has one durable profile that survives across teams/seasons; 'Career Stats' (baseball/softball) auto-tally 150+ lifetime stats and the operator simply checkmarks which seasons roll into a career. Box scores + play-by-play are free for coaches, view-gated to confirmed family/players otherwise. ACCESS for non-app-users: an Athlete Profile is a SHAREABLE LINK (text/email/social) — the recipient views the full profile (stats, clips, bio) with NO subscription of their own. Privacy is per-player ('confirmed family/players can view only the stats of their player' vs the whole team). Premium-gated.

products.name: MaxPreps (CBS Sports) — HS recruiting/records
products.howStatsWork: The HS stat system of record. Two entry paths: (1) head coach + staff enter stats in the Coach Admin (game-by-game OR cumulative 'Season-to-Date'); (2) MaxPreps IMPORTS from 80+ stat partners (incl. GameChanger) for football/basketball/volleyball/baseball/softball/lacrosse/water-polo/soccer — least-effort path. Crucial recruiting twist: a parent/player can CLAIM the athlete profile and self-enter stats IF the coach hasn't — but athlete-entered stats show ONLY on the career page, NOT on team pages, and are NOT leaderboard-eligible (anti-gaming). Athlete profiles are PUBLIC web pages built for recruiting; team/career/leaderboard pages are public and indexed.

products.name: Hudl + Hudl Assist
products.howStatsWork: Film-first. Coach records (Hudl Focus camera or capture device), uploads game, submits to Assist; human analysts (+ AI in some sports) tag EVERY team & individual stat for BOTH teams, 24/7 turnaround. Every data point is tied to video; filterable across multiple games/seasons. Identity: every athlete on a Hudl team gets a PUBLIC profile page with highlights, stats, scores — opt-in 'recruiting' exposes the profile + full game film to college coaches. The recruiting/college-coach reach is the stickiness moat.

products.name: SportsEngine (NBC Sports / NGIN)
products.howStatsWork: Team/league management with stats as one module. Team manager marks a game complete and enters per-game player + team stats in Scores & Stats; the platform AUTO-COMPILES season totals + standings from each game. Surfaced via configurable widgets (Roster, Schedule, Statistics, Standings, Stat Leaders) on the public Team Page. Parents view through the team page / SE Mobile app. Season is a first-class object ('Season Management' configures which stats + scoring settings apply).

products.name: Athletic.net (track & field / cross country)
products.howStatsWork: Event-result model, not counting-stats. Coaches/meet hosts/timers UPLOAD meet results (supports most electronic timing formats for auto-import); when a meet is marked OFFICIAL, team records + season records by athlete/event/grade auto-update. Athletes CLAIM their bio; once claimed, the system auto-finds every meet they ran and displays Personal Records (PRs) + Season Bests inline with results. Profiles + records lists are PUBLIC web pages. The PR / season-best progression chart is the emotional hook for the athlete.

products.name: TeamSnap
products.howStatsWork: Lightweight, fully CUSTOMIZABLE stat tracker — the team picks exactly which stats to track and the column order. Coach/manager enters player stats per game; the app shows player stats, team stats, team leaders, game stats. Visibility is a per-team toggle: stats can be public to all, or marked PRIVATE (managers only). No persistent cross-team athlete identity or recruiting layer — it is roster/communication-first.

products.name: PlayMetrics (club soccer OS)
products.howStatsWork: Club-operating-system; stats are part of a rich player profile (team assignments, positions, attendance, evaluations, game scores, training history). Parents ('Player Contacts') log into the player profile to view history, scores, evaluations and live-game chat. Access is a real authenticated parent/player ACCOUNT role rather than a shareable public link — privacy by login, scoped to the club.

dataModelPatterns: PERSISTENT ATHLETE IDENTITY decoupled from the per-game appearance is universal. Every leader (GameChanger 'Athlete', MaxPreps/Athletic.net claimable bio, Hudl/SE profile) has ONE durable athlete record that a per-game roster spot links to. VenueOS already mirrors this exactly: SportsPerson (durable) + RosterPlayer.personId (per-game appearance) + Team. The model is correct; the gap is entirely in WIRING + ACCESS, not schema.

SEASON IS A FIRST-CLASS, EXPLICIT OBJECT (or an athletic-year string the operator picks), never a bare calendar year. SportsEngine/Athletic.net treat 'Season' as a configured entity; GameChanger lets you checkmark which seasons aggregate. CODE GAP CONFIRMED: VenueOS deriveSeason() (sports-stats.service.ts:414) returns String(d.getFullYear()) i.e. '2026' — which mis-buckets winter sports that span Dec→Mar across two calendar years, and the schema's own comment/Team.season expect the '2025-26' athletic-year format. This silently splits a basketball season into two and is a high-priority correctness fix.

THREE-TIER ROLLUP: per-game stat line (box score) → season aggregate → career aggregate. VenueOS has season+career (PlayerSeasonStat/PlayerCareerStat, materialized + indexed, idempotent finalize on FINAL — all correct and wired at sports.service.ts:3344). The MISSING tier is the per-game GAME LOG / box-score read: RosterPlayer rows persist forever (gameId FK), so the raw data exists, but getAthleteCareer() only returns season+career and never the game-by-game line. Every competitor surfaces a game log; this is the cheapest high-value add (read-only, data already stored).

COUNTING vs RATE stat distinction. VenueOS already encodes this well (statSemantic 'counting' accumulates, rate stats like AVG/judged scores stay per-game and are never summed) — matches how the leaders compute career totals correctly. No gap here.

ANTI-GAMING / SOURCE-OF-TRUTH provenance. MaxPreps' rule (athlete-self-entered stats hit the career page but NOT team pages or leaderboards) is the model for trust. VenueOS' equivalent safeguard already exists structurally: only LINKED RosterPlayer rows (personId set) on OUR-team (isHome) roll up, so opponents/typos never pollute persistent tables. Keep this invariant if a future parent-claim/self-entry path is added.

EXTERNAL-ID HOOK for import/sync. SportsPerson.externalRef already exists as the forward hook for GameChanger/MaxPreps IDs — matches the reality that MaxPreps' dominant entry path is IMPORT from 80+ partners (incl. GameChanger), not manual entry. The least-effort future play is import, not asking operators to key stats.
entryPatterns: Least-effort entry wins, and the winners minimize it three ways: (1) DERIVE stats from play-by-play the scorekeeper already taps (GameChanger — 150+ stats from plays); (2) AUTO-TAG from film via humans+AI (Hudl Assist); (3) IMPORT from another system (MaxPreps from 80+ partners; Athletic.net from timing-system files). Manual per-stat typing (TeamSnap, SportsEngine) is the laggard pattern. VenueOS' advantage: it ALREADY captures per-game player stats live during the game via the console steppers — so the per-game line is free; the only operator action needed is LINKING the roster row to a durable athlete.

The athlete-link step is the real adoption risk and every leader removes it almost entirely. GameChanger/Athletic.net/MaxPreps use one persistent identity the roster auto-attaches to; the operator rarely re-identifies a player. VenueOS' link is currently a MANUAL one-tap-per-player-per-game button (RosterPanel LinkAthleteButton) with NO auto-match and NO readback (there's no linkedPersonId echoed on the roster query, so 'Linked' is only local state and is lost on refresh). The competitor pattern says: AUTO-MATCH by name+number within a Team across games (find-or-create already exists server-side via normalizedKey + tenant_person_identity unique) so linking happens once, or for the whole roster at import, not every game.

Season-to-Date as an alternative to game-by-game (MaxPreps) — a fallback for operators who don't run the live console. VenueOS doesn't need this because it captures live, but worth noting the leaders offer BOTH a live-derived and a bulk-cumulative path.

Mark-game-FINAL is the universal aggregation trigger (SportsEngine 'mark complete', GameChanger end-of-game, Athletic.net 'mark official'). VenueOS matches this exactly — finalizeGameStats fires on the FINAL status transition, post-commit, fail-open, idempotent. This piece is done correctly.

Roster IMPORT as the bulk on-ramp. Operators build the roster once (CSV/import), and the durable athletes are created then — linking is implicit. VenueOS has roster CRUD + import but creates per-game RosterPlayer rows without auto-creating/linking SportsPerson at import time; doing the find-or-create AT IMPORT (when teamId is known) would make every subsequent game auto-link for free.
accessPatterns: A SHAREABLE PUBLIC LINK to an athlete profile is the dominant access pattern, precisely because the audience (parents, grandparents, recruiters) are NOT logged-in dashboard users. GameChanger: share via text/email/social, recipient needs no subscription. MaxPreps/Athletic.net/Hudl: the athlete profile is a PUBLIC, indexable web page. CRITICAL VENUEOS GAP: every stat read endpoint — GET athletes/:id/career, GET leaders — is behind @RequireRoles (dashboard JWT). There is ZERO parent/player-facing surface and NO web page that renders career stats at all (no athlete/career/profile route exists under apps/web/src/app). A parent literally cannot see their kid's stats. This is the single biggest gap vs. the entire field.

The codebase ALREADY has the exact pattern to fix it: a public, no-auth, by-id-only SportsBoardController (GET /api/v1/sports/board/:id) with a public web route at apps/web/src/app/board/[gameId] (no [schoolId] auth prefix). Recommendation: mirror this for athletes — a public GET /api/v1/sports/board/athletes/:id (unguessable UUID = the capability token, same trust model the board already uses) + a public web page at apps/web/src/app/athlete/[personId]. Reuses an established, reviewed pattern; additive; no new auth system.

Per-player PRIVACY granularity matters (GameChanger 'view only my player' vs whole team; TeamSnap public-vs-managers-only toggle). For VenueOS multi-tenant + minors, recommend: profiles OFF by default, operator opts a team/athlete IN to public sharing, and the link is an unguessable UUID (not enumerable) — plus a per-athlete 'hide' flag. Privacy-by-default is the responsible posture for a K-12-rooted product.

The GAME LOG / box score is part of every profile (game-by-game line, not just totals). VenueOS stores the data (RosterPlayer per game) but never reads it back — add a getAthleteGameLog read alongside getAthleteCareer.

Recruiting is the high-end access driver (Hudl opt-in to college coaches; MaxPreps public recruiting profiles). Not needed for v1 but the natural premium tier — VenueOS' externalRef + public-profile foundation positions it for an export/share-to-recruiter feature later.

Push/recap engagement: GameChanger's pull is following the game when you can't attend (live stream + play-by-play + post-game stats). VenueOS already runs the live board/ribbon; a post-game auto-recap (email/SMS 'Here's [player]'s game: 18 PTS, 7 REB — view profile') would convert the existing live moment into a sticky after-game touch, mirroring why parents stay glued to GameChanger.
understand.stickiness: "Stickiness in this category comes from the ATHLETE + their family, not the operator. The platforms that win create a durable, emotionally-owned artifact for the kid — a lifetime stat profile, PR/season-best progression, highlight reel, recruiting page — that the family checks, shares, and would lose if they left. GameChanger is 'the app parents are obsessed with' because it lets a working parent follow the game live and own their child's stats + clips forever; Athletic.net hooks athletes with the PR progression chart; MaxPreps/Hudl hook families with public recruiting exposure to college coaches. The common mechanic: the more games played, the more irreplaceable the accumulated history becomes (switching cost compounds every season), and the shareable public link turns every parent/grandparent/recruiter into a distribution node at zero marketing cost. For VenueOS the strategic insight is that its CURRENT product is operator-facing only (the board on the gym wall); the stats engine is the lever to extend stickiness to the FAMILY — the largest, most loyal, most viral audience in school athletics — while the venue already, uniquely, captures every stat live during the game. The board earning its keep 5 days a week is the operator wedge; the athlete profile earning a family's loyalty for 4 years of high school is the consumer wedge."
understand.recommendation: "VERDICT: the data model is right and largely wired; the product is missing its entire consumer-facing half. finalizeGameStats IS wired (FINAL transition, gated by SPORTS_PLAYER_STATS, idempotent, fail-open) and season/career aggregation is correct. But the stats are invisible to the only audience that makes this sticky. Ship in this order: (P0 — the unlock) Build a PUBLIC athlete profile: an unauthenticated, by-UUID read endpoint (mirror the existing public SportsBoardController) + a public web page at apps/web/src/app/athlete/[personId], privacy-OFF-by-default with an operator opt-in-to-share toggle and an unguessable-UUID share link — this is the table-stakes feature every competitor has and VenueOS has zero of. (P0 — correctness) Fix deriveSeason() at sports-stats.service.ts:414 to emit an athletic-year string ('2025-26') for winter sports instead of a bare calendar year, before any real data accrues and mis-buckets a basketball season. (P1 — adoption) Make linking effortless: auto-find-or-create + auto-link SportsPerson by name+number within a Team at ROSTER IMPORT (the server already has find-or-create via normalizedKey), and echo linkedPersonId back on the roster query so the 'Linked' state is real and survives refresh — turn a per-game manual chore into a one-time setup. (P1 — completeness) Add a per-game GAME LOG read to getAthleteCareer (the RosterPlayer rows already persist; just read them back) so the profile shows game-by-game lines, not only totals. (P2 — stickiness multiplier) Post-game auto-recap (email/SMS with the player's line + profile link) to convert the live-game moment into a recurring family touch, the GameChanger habit loop. Keep the MaxPreps anti-gaming invariant (only LINKED, OUR-team rows aggregate). All of this is additive/nullable-schema-safe for the live pilot."

understand.entryFlow: Console UI (RosterPanel.tsx:372): PlayerEditorModal edits player name, number, position, photo, and flexible stat key-value pairs (6-row table seeded with sport-typical keys). POST /api/v1/sports/games/gameId/roster or PATCH updates send stats object to API. Persists to RosterPlayer.stats JSON column (schema.prisma lines 2159-2187). Post-game finalization triggered on game status=FINAL: finalizeGameStats() called from sports.service.ts line 3344 (wrapped in try-catch, fail-open, gated by SPORTS_PLAYER_STATS flag). Idempotent via game.stats.statsFinalizedAt marker. Engine (sports-stats.service.ts:569-731) rolls up only LINKED roster rows (personId is not null) and only COUNTING stats. Season derived from Game.startedAt or createdAt year (YYYY string). Upserts into PlayerSeasonStat (personId,season,statKey aggregate) and PlayerCareerStat (recomputed from all seasons).
understand.accessModel: Three access paths: (1) Admin console (authed CONTRIBUTOR+): GET /sports/leaders?sport=X&statKey=Y&scope=SEASON|CAREER&season=YYYY&limit=N for cross-game leaderboards; GET /sports/athletes/:id/career for one athlete full history (sports.controller.ts:1025-1072). (2) Public board /board/gameId (unauthenticated): per-game stat leaders and player-of-game computed live from roster (computePlayerSurfaces, read-only). (3) Public athlete career portal (NOT YET BUILT): could reuse getAthleteCareer() for /athletes/personId/career public route matching existing /board pattern. Privacy constraint: public athlete portal must not expose full name, contact, grad year without parental consent model.
understand.seasonScoping: Additive schema: Team.season nullable column (schema.prisma:2395-2421) stores academic year like 2025-26. Game model has no season column; deriveSeason() function (sports-stats.service.ts:508) computes YYYY from Game.startedAt or Game.createdAt. PlayerSeasonStat table has unique constraint on (personId, season, statKey) (schema.prisma:2455-2478). Future refinement: use Team.season='2025-26' for academic-year filtering; add optional Game.season column for explicit season assignment instead of calendar-year derivation.
understand.privacy: Minor athlete PII: RosterPlayer.name, number, position, photoUrl are game-context public (visible on scoreboard). SportsPerson.fullName, firstName, lastName, gradYear are PRIVATE (admin console only). Public athlete portal design: do not expose full name, contact info, or grad year without explicit parental consent framework. Safer approach: show only jersey number or nickname plus stats, no identifying details.
reusable: getAthleteCareer() (sports-stats.service.ts:840) reads aggregates; ready for public /athletes/personId/career route
linkRosterPlayerToPerson() (lines:418-550) handles find-or-create athlete linking by name or explicit personId
POST /sports/games/:id/roster/:rosterPlayerId/link endpoint (sports.controller.ts:1004) wires operator link UI to database
deriveSeason() (line:508) stable season derivation; idempotence safe for re-finalize
computePlayerSurfaces() (Phase-1 leaders/POTG) serves public board stat display
finalizeGameStats() already WIRED to setStatus(FINAL) hook (sports.service.ts:3344); idempotent, fail-open pattern in place

designs.oneLineSummary: Wire finalizeGameStats to FINAL (already done), auto-link athletes at import, public athlete profiles with game logs
designs.dataModel: No new tables. Reuse SportsPerson (persistent athlete), RosterPlayer (per-game appearance with nullable personId), PlayerSeasonStat, PlayerCareerStat. Additive schema: SportsPerson.publicShareToken (UUID capability, optional), SportsPerson.sharePublic (boolean, default false). Optional Game.season for academic-year override (P2).
designs.entryUX: Operator imports CSV at season start (one-time): POST /roster/import auto-creates SportsPerson by normalizedKey within team, sets personId on all rows. Live console edits stats per game. On FINAL, finalizeGameStats triggers (already wired), rolls up counting stats idempotently to season + career aggregates.
designs.finalizeWiring: IMPLEMENTED. sports.service.ts setStatus() lines 3338-3359: finalizeGameStats wrapped try/catch, fail-open, SPORTS_PLAYER_STATS gated. Only LINKED rows aggregate. Idempotent via game.stats.statsFinalizedAt marker. No changes needed; optional ?_finalize=true query for backfill.
designs.accessSurface: PUBLIC ENDPOINT: GET /api/v1/sports/board/athletes/:publicShareToken (unauthed, token-gated, 10 req/min/IP). PUBLIC PAGE: /athlete/[token] (unauthenticated, responsive). Shows athlete bio, season stats table, career stats, game log (most recent first). Privacy: off by default; operator opts athlete in per-sport via roster settings. Share button generates link for parent/grandparent.

P2 FIX: add Game.season override column; when set, use it; else derive. Operator can opt-in to academic year (2025-26) per team.

designs.liveSafety: 100% additive schema (nullable columns only). No breaking changes to Game, RosterPlayer, or game flow. Existing pilot tenants unaffected: Phase 2 gated by SPORTS_PLAYER_STATS flag (off by default). Finalization fail-open: if finalizeGameStats errors, game stays FINAL, error logged, stats best-effort (not required). Public profile has no auth/identity needed (same /board model). Roster import backward compatible; new find-or-create is post-import idempotent.

designs.approachName: GameChanger-Parity Athlete Platform: Complete Player-Stats Engine with Public Consumer Access
designs.oneLineSummary: Bridge the verified but invisible player-stats engine to families via a public athlete profile + game log with GameChanger-style stickiness, fixed season definition, and effortless linking at roster import.
designs.dataModel:
Additive, nullable schema only (live-pilot safe):

CORE PERSISTENCE (verified in schema, wired at sports.service.ts:3344):
  - Team: sport, season (nullable "2025-26"), isHome, colorPrimary, logoUrl
  - SportsPerson: fullName, firstName, lastName, number, position, photoUrl, gradYear, normalizedKey (dedup), externalRef (GameChanger/MaxPreps forward hook)
  - RosterPlayer: personId (FK SportsPerson, nullable), teamId (FK Team, nullable), stats (JSON, flexible)
  - PlayerSeasonStat: (personId, season, statKey) unique, statValue (float), gamesPlayed (int), displayValue (formatted), lastGameId (traces to source game)
  - PlayerCareerStat: (personId, statKey) unique, same shape as season (recomputed across all seasons inside finalize tx)

REQUIRED ADDITIVE MODELS:
  1. AthleteProfile: personId (FK), visibility (OFF|ON_DEMAND|PUBLIC), shareableUuid (unguessable), photoUrl (prominent large), bioBlurb (opt), isActive, createdAt, updatedAt. Unique on (tenantId, personId).
  2. AthleteGameLog: no new table (reuse RosterPlayer rows with personId set + Game join). Query by person_id, order by game.startedAt DESC. Each row is one game's box score (stats JSON).
  3. Season model (lightweight reference, not strict enforcement): Season (tenantId, sport, year/range "2025-26", label, startDate, endDate). Optional — drives UI grouping and academic-calendar correctness. Soft reference from Game + Team via string enum.

SEASON DEFINITION CORRECTNESS (P0 bug fix):
  - Current: deriveSeason(game) returns bare calendar year "2026" (line 414, sports-stats.service.ts), mis-bucketing winter sports that span Dec→Mar across two calendar years.
  - Fix: emit academic-year string like "2025-26" by:
    1. Add optional Game.season (nullable string, e.g. "2025-26"), set at game-create time via the operator-picked Team.season or a sensible default.
    2. deriveSeason() prefers Game.season if set, else falls back to calendar-year derivation (backward-compatible).
    3. Emit "YYYY-YY" (e.g. "2025-26") when no explicit Game.season: if startedAt.month >= 9 (Sept), emit `${year}-${year+1 % 100}`; else emit `${year-1}-${year % 100}`.
    4. PlayerSeasonStat rows created with "2025-26" not split into "2025" + "2026".

PUBLIC ACCESS SURFACE (missing entirely; table-stakes):
  1. New public endpoint: GET /api/v1/sports/board/athletes/:shareableUuid (unguessable capability token, no auth required, returns minimal PII: number/nickname, stats, grad year only if parental opt-in). 404 if visibility!=ON_DEMAND and not the sharing operator's session.
  2. New public web page: apps/web/src/app/athlete/[shareableUuid]/page.tsx (unauthenticated, renders profile card + season leaderboard rank + game log + career card).
  3. Privacy: AthleteProfile.visibility OFF by default; operator explicitly toggles per-athlete (Settings → Athlete Profiles → [player] ON or Share Link). When ON, link is unguessable UUID + expires optional, never enumerable by player id.

MATERIALIZATION + FINALIZE (verified working, wired, idempotent):
  - finalizeGameStats (sports-stats.service.ts:569): fired on Game.status=FINAL (sports.service.ts:3344), post-commit, wrapped try/catch fail-open. Idempotent via game.stats.statsFinalizedAt marker inside tx. Only LINKED roster rows (personId set, isHome=true on team) aggregate. Counting stats only (rate stats like AVG never summed). Career recomputed from all season rows inside the tx (canonical). Multi-replica safe (first to commit marker wins).
designs.entryUX:
TWO-PHASE ADOPTION (operator zero-friction):

PHASE 1 — ROSTER IMPORT (one-time, bulk auto-link):
  1. Operator downloads CSV template (existing flow, RosterPanel.tsx:59-79).
  2. Fills in team+name+number+stats columns.
  3. Clicks Import CSV (existing).
  4. NEW: Server-side enhancement at import-time (sports.controller.ts roster-import handler):
     - For each CSV row: call linkRosterPlayerToPerson({ tenantId, rosterPlayerId, fullName, teamId }) where teamId is the operator-picked Team entity (not a free-text string).
     - find-or-create SportsPerson by (tenantId, teamId, normalizedKey, gradYear=null) within the same tx.
     - Update RosterPlayer.personId + RosterPlayer.teamId in the same tx.
     - Result: every roster row is auto-linked at import time. Operator never sees a "Link" button; it's implicit.
  5. Rollback on FK error (teamId invalid) — operator is prompted to pick a Team before import.

PHASE 2 — LIVE CONSOLE (manual fallback for mid-game additions):
  - LinkAthleteButton (RosterPanel.tsx:318-370) remains for one-off players added during the game.
  - Renamed hint: "Link to persistent athlete (season + career stats)" → "Auto-link to athlete." Button latches local state "Linked ✓" (already implemented).
  - Echo linkedPersonId back on roster query (small API change, RosterPanel re-query shows real persisted state, survives refresh). Operator confidence signal.

LINKING INVARIANT (anti-gaming):
  - Only LINKED roster rows (personId != null) aggregate at finalize.
  - Only OUR-TEAM roster rows (Team.isHome=true, or Game.homeTeamId matches) roll up to persistent tables.
  - Opponents/typos/one-off players never pollute season/career tables (structure guarantees it).
  - When a person is deleted, RosterPlayer.personId SetNull → row becomes unlinked (survives as a game record, just stops rolling up).
designs.finalizeWiring:
VERIFIED + WORKING, NO CHANGES NEEDED except Season definition:

1. Game.status transitions to FINAL (sports.service.ts:3283-3360).
2. Inside setStatus() post-commit, wrapped try/catch:
   ```typescript
   const result = await finalizeGameStats(this.prisma.client, tenantId, id);
   ```
3. finalizeGameStats (sports-stats.service.ts:569):
   - Load game tenant-scoped, derive season.
   - Find all LINKED roster rows (WHERE personId IS NOT NULL).
   - For each LINKED player, extract COUNTING stat deltas only (rate stats excluded by design).
   - Upsert PlayerSeasonStat (personId, season, statKey) → add delta to statValue, bump gamesPlayed.
   - Recompute PlayerCareerStat from all season rows for that (personId, statKey).
   - Stamp idempotency marker game.stats.statsFinalizedAt inside tx (replay-safe).
   - Return { aggregated: count_of_linked_players }.
4. Fail-open: if error thrown, caught and logged by caller, game row unaffected (status already FINAL).
5. Idempotency: re-FINAL returns { aggregated: 0, skipped: 'already-finalized' }, double-counts zero.

SEASON FIX (P0, add to finalize call):
  - Before upsert: call fixed deriveSeason(game) that emits "2025-26" not "2026".
  - Backfill script (one-time): for every PlayerSeasonStat row where season = bare year AND the linked RosterPlayer's game spans Dec→Mar, recalculate + move to correct academic year (or null out + re-finalize the game post-fix).

pros: Data model already correct + wired (finalizeGameStats idempotent, fail-open, called on FINAL, verified by line traces).
Per-game stat lines already persisted (RosterPlayer.stats JSON) — game log is a trivial read, not a rebuild.
Linking infrastructure exists (linkRosterPlayerToPerson find-or-create) — just move from manual per-game to auto at import.
Public board pattern already proven (sports-board-cache, no-auth endpoint, unguessable UUID) — reuse for athlete profile.
Season definition fix is a 4-line function change (deriveSeason) + optional Game.season column, no major refactor.
Additive schema only (AthleteProfile, Season optional, RosterPlayer.personId/teamId already nullable) — live pilot safe.
Privacy-by-default (visibility OFF, operator opt-in per athlete) — responsible for K-12 / minors.
Anti-gaming structure built-in (only linked OUR-team rows aggregate) — no new validation needed.
Stickiness multiplier unlocked (game log + season rank + career totals visible to family) — mirrors GameChanger/MaxPreps/Athletic.net.
Recruitment pathway open (externalRef already exists for GameChanger/MaxPreps ID sync) — future export/import.
Post-game engagement hook (email/SMS with player's line + profile link) — habit loop identical to GameChanger's winning mechanic.
cons: Season string handling: winter sports split into two calendar years under current deriveSeason (P0 fix required before real data accrues; backfill possible but messy if data exists).
Roster import refactor needed to auto-link at CSV import time (small, localizes to RosterPanel.tsx + sports.controller import handler, but touching CRUD flow requires careful test).
Public athlete endpoint exposes PII (name, photo, grad year) when visibility=ON — requires clear operator opt-in UX (mitigated by ON_DEMAND default + per-athlete toggle).
Game log query performance: if a player has 100+ games (multi-season), the list is long; pagination could be deferred to P1 (load first 20, paginate on demand).
Share-link generation: if operator accidentally toggles profile ON/OFF repeatedly, old links orphan (not a breaking issue, just a UX papercut; link becomes 404, which is safe).

No athlete self-claim (parent can't add themselves to their kid's profile) — only operator can publish. Justifiable for pilot (operator control, no account signup needed for parents); future: parent claim flow via email invite.
Migration from bare-year seasons to 'YYYY-YY' requires operator awareness (can coexist, but leaderboards show both; light education in release notes).
Leaderboard tie-breaking on same stat value is undefined (same rank shown; cosmetic, could add games-played secondary sort later).

designs.dataModel:
ADDITIVE SCHEMA (nullable, pilot-safe):

1. SportsPerson.isPublic: bool @default(false) 
   – Operator opt-in to share this athlete's profile publicly. Defaults OFF (privacy-by-default for minors).

2. SportsPerson.publicShareToken: string? @unique
   – Unguessable UUID (e.g., crypto.randomUUID()) for the shareable link. Regenatable by operator.
   – Pattern: /api/v1/sports/athletes/{publicShareToken}/career (unauthed, by-UUID-only, no name enumerable).

3. Team.season: string? (already in schema as e.g. '2025-26')
   – Fixes deriveSeason() to emit academic-year strings for winter sports (currently broken: returns bare '2026').

4. SportsPerson.personIdForLink: string? @map("person_id_for_link") DEPRECATED
   – NOT a new column: RosterPanel's local state `setLinked(true)` should echo linkedPersonId from the roster refresh, making link persistence real instead of local UI lie.

DATA FLOW:

Per-Game Entry (console, today):
  1. Operator enters per-game RosterPlayer stats (PlayerEditorModal, stats JSON).
  2. At import time: for each roster row with fullName + number, call linkRosterPlayerToPerson() server-side (find-or-create SportsPerson by normalizedKey within tenant+team).
  3. Result: RosterPlayer.personId is SET at import, not later via one-tap.
  4. No manual per-game "Link" button needed after import.

Game Finalization (FINAL status):
  – finalizeGameStats() fires (already wired in sports.service.ts:3344, post-commit, fail-open).
  – Rolls up ONLY LINKED rows (personId is not null) using deriveSeason(game).
  – Upserts PlayerSeasonStat + PlayerCareerStat (indexed, materialized).
  – Season derivation: if Game.season is set, use it; else calendar year from startedAt/createdAt (fix below).

Public Profile Read:
  – GET /api/v1/sports/athletes/{publicShareToken}/career (unauthed SportsBoardController sibling).
  – Returns AthleteCareer: fullName, number, position, photo, team, grad_year + game-by-game log + season + career stats.
  – ONLY if SportsPerson.isPublic=true.

"
designs.entryUX:
OPERATOR ONBOARDING: Roster Import (One-Time, Per-Season)

Flow:
  1. Coach uploads CSV (today's flow: POST /games/:id/roster/import).
  2. Server finds-or-creates Team + SportsPerson rows AT IMPORT (not later).
  3. For each CSV row [Name, Number, Position, Photo, Stats]:
     – Call findOrCreateAthlete(tenantId, teamId, name, number, …) server-side.
     – Returns personId; link RosterPlayer.personId = personId immediately.
     – Result: every game's roster is pre-linked on import. No "Link" button needed after.
  4. Operator toggles "Public Profile" on the Team → SportsPerson settings (batch per team).
     – Generates publicShareToken for each opted-in athlete.
     – Share link is: venue-os.app/athlete/{publicShareToken}

Per-Game Console (Today's Flow, Unchanged):
  1. RosterPanel.tsx shows the roster with stat steppers.
  2. LinkAthleteButton is REMOVED (linking already happened at import).
  3. Operator edits stats as normal.
  4. On status=FINAL, finalizeGameStats() auto-runs.

Post-Game Share (New):
  1. Coach taps "Share Game Stats" → generates a recap image/email with highlights:
     – "Game: VH Basketball @ Lincoln | Jan 15, 2026"
     – Top 3 stat leaders (3 short lines)
     – Athlete profiles: "View {Player Name}'s Season Stats → [link to /athlete/{token}]"
  2. Email sends to parents (operator copy-paste email list, or SIS integration future).
  3. Family clicks link → unauthenticated profile page (name, photo, season stats, game log, career).

EASIEST OPERATOR ENTRY:
  – Import CSV once per season → automatic linking for all games that season.
  – No manual per-game "Link" button friction.
  – Operator only re-links if a player is added mid-season (add to Team, relink that row in-game, OR add to CSV + re-import).

"

designs.seasonModel:
DEFINITION (Consistent Across All Features):
  – A Season is an ACADEMIC YEAR: "2025-26", "2026-27", …
  – Spans calendar year 1 (e.g. Aug 2025 → Dec 2025) + calendar year 2 (e.g. Jan 2026 → Jun 2026).
  – Eliminates the winter-sport split where a Jan 2026 game incorrectly falls into two separate "2025" + "2026" season rows.

SCHEMA:
  – Team.season: string? nullable (e.g. "2025-26" or null for perennial programs).
  – Game.season: string? nullable (optional explicit assignment; defaults to deriveSeason(game)).
  – PlayerSeasonStat.season: string NOT NULL (e.g. "2025-26").
  – deriveSeason() returns Game.season if set, else falls back to calendar year from startedAt/createdAt.

OPERATOR FLOW:
  1. Pre-game: Coach creates Team with season="2026-27" (or season=null for multi-year program).
  2. Per-game: Game inherits Team.season by default (or explicit Game.season override, rare).
  3. On FINAL: finalizeGameStats uses deriveSeason(game) → "2026-27".
  4. Finalize upserts PlayerSeasonStat(personId, season='2026-27', statKey, …).
  5. Post-season: New Team(season='2027-28') is created for next year. Old team's season is frozen at '2026-27'.

MULTI-YEAR ATHLETES (e.g., a grad-year-2028 athlete plays 2024-25, 2025-26, 2026-27):
  – PlayerSeasonStat has a row per season (2024-25, 2025-26, 2026-27, …).
  – PlayerCareerStat is the sum of ALL seasons (no season field, only statKey).
  – Profile shows tabs: [2026-27] [2025-26] [2024-25] with individual totals + career totals at bottom.

"
pros: EXISTING DATA MODEL IS CORRECT — SportsPerson (persistent athlete), Team (program), RosterPlayer.personId (per-game link), PlayerSeasonStat, PlayerCareerStat (materialized aggregates) are all in place. No schema rebuild needed.
FINALIZE-ON-FINAL IS ALREADY WIRED — finalizeGameStats() is called post-status-FINAL, wrapped fail-open, idempotent, gated by flag. Just verified in code.
OPERATOR FRICTION ELIMINATED — One roster import at season start auto-links all players. No per-game manual 'Link' button. Matches how every leader does it (auto-link happens once per athlete).
FAMILY REACHES STATS WITHOUT LOGIN — Public /athlete/{token} page mirrors the public /board/{gameId} pattern (existing, proven, reviewed). No new auth system. Unguessable UUID = capability token.
PRIVACY-BY-DEFAULT — Profiles OFF by default. Operator opts-in per athlete. No minors' details exposed without consent.
GAME LOG IS FREE — RosterPlayer rows already persist per-game. Just query them back (WHERE personId ORDER BY gameId/game.createdAt). No new table needed.
ANTI-GAMING INVARIANT PRESERVED — Only LINKED, OUR-team (isHome=true) rows aggregate. Opponents/typos never pollute persistent tables.
SEASON FIX IS CORRECTNESS WIN — Winter sports no longer split across two years. Academic-year strings unblock future 'seasonal' features (grades, events, scholarships).
ZERO NEW INFRASTRUCTURE — All reads hit indexed materialized tables (fast, no recompute). No caching layer, no CRON, no async queue.

PILOT-SAFE, ADDITIVE SCHEMA — SportsPerson.isPublic nullable bool. SportsPerson.publicShareToken nullable unique. Game.season nullable. Existing games/athletes unaffected. Feature can ship behind a flag.
cons: LINKING AT IMPORT REQUIRES CSV SCHEMA ALIGNMENT — Coach must provide Name + Number in CSV matching the persistent Team's athletes. If CSV is malformed or athlete names diverge (nickname vs. full name), find-or-create may create duplicates. Mitigation: validate + preview CSV before import, show 'Matched / Unmatched' count.

SEASON DERIVATION FIX BREAKS EXISTING PILOT DATA — If pilot has games in 2025 + 2026 mixed in one season, recalculating deriveSeason will silently shuffle rows. Mitigation: (a) run a one-time migration to explicitly set Game.season for all pilot games before deploying the fix, OR (b) deprecate the old calendar-year rows and regenerate from RosterPlayer deltas.

NO GAME-BY-GAME STAT LINE IN THE INITIAL RESPONSE — getAthleteCareer returns season+career, but the game-log query is separate. Requires a second API call or a JOIN. Mitigation: optional ?includeGameLog query param, or a separate /athletes/{token}/game-log endpoint.
COACH-ROSTER-HUB UI NOT SHIPPED IN THIS PHASE — /teams/[teamId]/roster-stats is nice-to-have but not critical (operator can see seasonal totals in leaderboards). Defer to Phase 2.

MULTI-TENANT TEAM IDENTITY IS STILL WEAK — Game.homeTeam and Game.awayTeam are free-text strings, not Team FKs. If a coach re-names 'Varsity' to 'Varsity Boys', the old team's name doesn't update everywhere. Mitigation: None in this phase; defer Team unification to a later schema cleanup.

PUBLIC PROFILE PAGE HAS MINIMAL BRANDING — Operator can't fully customize the athlete-profile template (colors, fonts, layout). Reuses basic VenueOS styles. Mitigation: future v2 allows operator to pick a profile template (like scoreboard builder).

NO MILESTONE/RECORD WIRING IN THIS PHASE — StatRecord, StatMilestoneDef, PlayerMilestone tables exist but finalizeGameStats doesn't trigger them. 'School Record!' celebrations won't fire. Mitigation: defer to Phase 3 (would add 1-2 days of work).

EMAIL RECAP NOT BUILT — Post-game 'Share Stats with Family' email requires Twilio/SMTP config + SIS integration (get parent emails from student ID). Mitigation: manual copy-paste link in v1; auto-send is Phase 2.
NO RECRUITING-PROFILE EXPORT (Hudl/MaxPreps Parity) — Platform doesn't auto-sync to recruiting sites. Mitigation: future feature; externalRef hook is in place for 2-way sync.

PRIVACY CONSENT MODEL NOT IMPLEMENTED — No parental consent form workflow. Operator manually decides per-athlete. Mitigation: sufficient for v1 (operator is responsible); future FERPA-audit tier can add e-sign + audit logs.

   ✓ Revert isPublic flag to false on all athletes (disables all public pages).
   ✓ publicShareToken is not cached; revoking is instant.
   ✓ No data loss — season/career tables remain, just hidden from public.

9. OPERATOR COMMUNICATION:
   ✓ Coach must understand: (1) import CSV once per season, (2) link is automatic, (3) toggle 'Public Profile' to enable share links.
   ✓ In-app onboarding message: 'Roster imported with 12 athletes linked. Profiles are private by default — opt-in on each athlete to enable sharing.'
   ✓ Help docs: CSV schema, public-profile feature, privacy model.

PRODUCTION READINESS: READY TO SHIP.
  – Existing infrastructure (finalizeGameStats, materialized tables) is in place.
  – New code is isolated (public endpoint, web page, import-time linking).
  – Schema is additive.
  – Rollback is clean.
  – Privacy is conservative (OFF by default).

synthesis.chosenApproach: Merge Design 2 (GameChanger-parity athlete platform) as the spine but drop its two heaviest schema additions, a full AthleteProfile table and a first-class Season table, in favor of the minimal nullable columns from Designs 1 and 3. We complete the existing engine, not rebuild it. Four shippable slices. S0 auto-link athletes at roster import plus echo the linked person id to the console. S1 public token-gated athlete profile endpoint plus web page plus share toggle. S2 game-log read reusing data already in RosterPlayer rows. S3 academic-season fix in deriveSeason plus an optional Game.season column. No new tables, only nullable columns on SportsPerson and Game.
synthesis.rationale: All three designs agree the data model is correct and finalizeGameStats is already wired, and I verified both. Finalize fires on FINAL at sports.service.ts lines 3343 to 3344, post-commit, try catch fail-open, SPORTS_PLAYER_STATS gated, idempotent via the game.stats.statsFinalizedAt marker checked at sports-stats.service.ts 598 and stamped at 716 to 727. The real work is the consumer half, not the engine. The differentiator between designs is schema weight. Design 2 adds a new AthleteProfile table and a new Season table. Designs 1 and 3 add SportsPerson.isPublic plus publicShareToken. Visibility and share-token state is one-to-one with the athlete so it belongs on SportsPerson; a separate AthleteProfile table buys nothing and adds a join plus migration risk on a live pilot. A full Season entity is over-build too: the only defect is deriveSeason returning a bare calendar year at sports-stats.service.ts 414 to 424; a string fix plus an optional Game.season override column corrects winter-sport splitting with zero new tables. I keep Design 2 stronger privacy framing, off by default, minor-PII caution, unguessable token, instant revoke, but on the leanest schema. The access surface mirrors an already-proven pattern: SportsBoardController at sports-board.controller.ts is deliberately unauthed, by-unguessable-uuid, with in-memory per-key rate limiting, so I clone it for athletes rather than inventing a new auth model.
synthesis.whatExistsVsNeeded: ALREADY EXISTS, completing not rebuilding. Correct three-table identity model: SportsPerson persistent athlete at schema.prisma 2423 to 2450, RosterPlayer.personId and teamId nullable per-game link at 2159 to 2191, PlayerSeasonStat at 2455 to 2475 plus PlayerCareerStat at 2479 to 2498, materialized aggregates with the right uniques and a sport season statKey statValue desc leaderboard index. Finalize on FINAL fully wired and idempotent at sports.service.ts 3338 to 3358, engine at sports-stats.service.ts 569 to 733; only LINKED our-roster rows aggregate, counting stats accumulate while rate stats stay per-game via the statSemantic gate at line 628, career recomputed and summed from season rows each finalize at 685 to 712 so it self-heals. Find-or-create linking: linkRosterPlayerToPerson at sports-stats.service.ts 440 to 552 by normalizedKey within tenant and team; endpoint POST sports games roster link at sports.controller.ts 1004 to 1023. Career read: getAthleteCareer at sports-stats.service.ts 840 to 916, AthleteCareer type 360 to 381. listRoster at sports.service.ts 1199 to 1205 already returns personId on every row, no select filter, so link-state readback is free. Game has homeTeamId and awayTeamId Team FKs plus free-text homeTeam and awayTeam plus homeScore, awayScore, startedAt. The exact public surface to clone: SportsBoardController unauthed by uuid plus rate limit, web routes app board gameId and app ribbon gameId. ACTUALLY MISSING, the consumer half. 1 Zero public access surface: getAthleteCareer is JWT and RBAC gated, no athlete web route, a parent literally cannot reach their kid stats; biggest gap vs every competitor. 2 No game-log read: RosterPlayer per-game rows persist forever but getAthleteCareer never reads them back, AthleteCareer has no gameLog field. 3 Linking is a manual one-tap-per-player-per-game chore: importRosterCsv at sports.service.ts 1313 to 1375 only createMany unlinked rows and never calls linkRosterPlayerToPerson, and RosterPanel.tsx 312 to 318 admits the Linked state is local-only, no linked person id echoed, so it is lost on refresh. 4 deriveSeason returns a bare calendar year so winter sports Dec to Mar split across two season rows. 5 No privacy controls: SportsPerson has no isPublic or share-token columns.
synthesis.accessAndPrivacy: Privacy-by-default capability-token model, responsible for a K-12-rooted product handling minors. Off by default: SportsPerson.isPublic false means the public endpoint returns 404 and the link is dead; an athlete is never exposed until an operator, SCHOOL_ADMIN or higher or CONTRIBUTOR, explicitly toggles share on. Capability token not id: access is GET api v1 sports board athletes publicShareToken where the token is an unguessable uuid, no enumeration by person id, mirrors the unguessable game-id trust model the public board already relies on at sports-board.controller.ts 12 to 14. Instant revoke: DELETE share sets isPublic false, endpoint 404s at once, and rotation re-issues a fresh token, orphaning any shared link. Minimal PII: payload defaults to number, position, photo, team plus stats; full name and grad year returned only because the operator opted in to share; a future per-athlete hide-name and grad-year flag is the next step. Anti-gaming invariant preserved: only LINKED our-roster rows aggregate, finalize where personId not null at sports-stats.service.ts 607, so opponents and typos never reach the persistent tables or the public profile. Rate-limited and auditable: in-memory per-token limit on the public read, clone of the feed limiter, every share on off or rotate writes an AuditLog row. Authed reads unchanged: getAthleteCareer and leaders stay JWT and RBAC for the coach console; the public path is a separate, narrower projection.

risks: Migration on a live pilot: two new nullable SportsPerson columns plus one nullable Game.season, all additive and nullable so existing rows are untouched, but per repo convention generate with prisma create-only and have the lead apply on merge, same discipline as the SponsorImpression note at schema.prisma 2264, never auto-push.

PII exposure of minors, the central risk: mitigated by off-by-default isPublic, unguessable token, instant revoke, minimal default payload, and an AuditLog on every share toggle; recommend an explicit operator confirm before first share-on.

deriveSeason format change is observable: new finalizes write YYYY-YY while old pilot rows may hold a bare year; they coexist, leaderboards filter by exact season string, no data loss, but an in-flight winter season could show two buckets; ship S3 before real winter data accrues; if any exists, a one-time re-key of Dec to Mar rows is clean-up, not a launch blocker.

Auto-link false matches at import: find-or-create keys on normalizedKey within tenant and team so a nickname versus fullname mismatch can spawn a duplicate SportsPerson; mitigate with a matched and unmatched preview count in the import response and keep the manual link as the correction path; only home rows auto-link.

Public endpoint load and abuse: an unauthed route invites scraping; the in-memory per-token rate limit is single-replica only, same caveat as the existing feed limiter, acceptable for launch, promote to Redis if it becomes load-bearing per the CLAUDE.md multi-replica caveat.
Cross-browser: a brand-new public DOM and poll surface must pass the WebKit smoke before done per the CLAUDE.md cross-browser rule, do not ship Chrome-only.
